correctness.rationale: Exact Krylov polynomial representation at simple Ritz nodes; strict Ritz top endpoint inequality from the support-cardinality polynomial argument; Newton divided difference and Hermite-Genocchi simplex remainder yield p_t(x)/exp(-tx)=1-(-1)^m H_m. For x above all Ritz nodes H_m is strictly increasing from 0 to infinity in t and strictly increasing in x. Hence odd m has no extreme-mode zero; even m has exactly one crossing, strictly decreasing in x. The Lagrange leading coefficient proves the relative-error asymptotic. Check.py (embedded as verify.py) tested m=1..7 in exact machine form for three input matrices and returned VERIFY_OK 16, corroborating but not proving infinite statements.

originality.rationale: The prior exact result covers two-step Lanczos only, with explicit m>=3 exclusion; the full mathematical presentation was read. The source Lanczos-FA paper gives the algorithmic representation but no all-depth sign theorem; the classical divided-difference representation is acknowledged as prior. The new implication is a for-all-m parity law and sole highest-mode zero at any even incomplete depth, with strict spectral ordering and odd-mode relative-error asymptotic; neither a special case of the m=2 result nor an algorithmic reformulation of it. No equivalent was identified in dedicated semantic, published-text, and own-claim searches; equivalence under unsearched terminology remains possible.

value.rationale: The object is a standard incomplete Krylov approximation to a positivity-preserving physical semigroup. The full-depth parity classification shows an intrinsic alternating obstruction: all odd truncation depths protect the stiffest coordinate, whereas all even truncation depths force a unique sign reversal. The strict ordering of high-mode crossing times and the exponentially bad relative error even at sign-protected odd depths are structural features relevant to interpreting positivity-preserving matrix-function computations. It goes beyond an arbitrary fixed numerical instance and gives a natural exact classification over every admissible dimension, but does not imply all-coordinate positivity.
